questions.question: At which Olympic Games did India win a gold medal for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928 Amsterdam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Indian men's hockey team **clinched their **first Olympic gold medal** in the **1928 Amsterdam Olympics.**
 
• This marked the beginning of India's long dominance in the field of hockey. It was **a highly symbolic achievement** spotlighting India's potential in international sports.
 
• The team did not concede a single goal across five matches, and they scored a total of 29 goals, establishing their supremacy in the tournament.
 
• Notably,** Major Dhyan Chand,** one of India's most legendary hockey players, played a pivotal role and **scored a hat-trick in the finals** against the **Netherlands.**
 
• This historic win initiated India's golden era in hockey, with the Indian team **securing six consecutive golds** in the Olympics from **1928 to 1956.**
 
• The Indian hockey men’s team has won eight Olympic gold medals in all, six of them in a row (from 1928-1956) and added two more at Tokyo 1964 and Moscow 1980.

questions.question: Identify the black soil region of India from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan trap.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Deccan trap,** located in the **central and western parts of India,** is a major region where **black soil **is found.
 
• This soil is typically black due to the** high concentration of metallic compounds and minerals**, particularly iron compounds, that it contains.
 
• Black soil, also known as** 'Regur' or 'Cotton Soil'**, is ideal for growing cotton and is hence named so.
 
• The soil has a** high capacity to hold moisture and is very fertile**, making it suitable for agriculture, particularly for the production of **cash crops like cotton, sugarcane, and soybeans.**
 
• **Besides the Deccan trap**, black soil can also be found in **Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, parts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Rajasthan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/259a2ec264895f096e5ef546cd7870524fbf524cf5ead589be36b1bf9f915fbd.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is the most widely spread and important soil in India, covering about 40% of the land area.
 
• It is highly fertile and rich in potash, phosphoric acid, and lime which are ideal for the growth of sugarcane, paddy, wheat, and other cereal and pulse crops.
 
• These soils are extensively found in Northern plains and river valleys.
 
• They are derived from the depositional work of rivers and are replenished every year by floods.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil:**
 
 
• Red soil covers about 24% of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• These soils are mainly found in the low rainfall regions of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and some parts of Tamil Nadu.
 
• They are rich in iron and potash but have less phosphoric content.
 
• Horticultural crops like oranges, figs, olives, and grapes are grown on a large scale in areas with red soils.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil, or Regur Soil:**
 
 
• Black soils cover about 15% of India, mainly in the Deccan Plateau.
 
• They are rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, lime, and are ideally suited for growing cotton.
 
• Also known as "Cotton Soil" due to its ability to retain moisture, it's prevalent in the states of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• They are found in high rainfall and temperature areas of the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Northeast states, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• They are characterized by heavy leaching due to high rainfall which leads to the leaching away of siliceous material and lime of the rocks and leaves behind oxides of iron and aluminum.
 
• Such soils are suitable for cultivating plantations of cashew, tea, coffee, rubber, and coconut.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnam Malleswari.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnam Malleswari** is the **first Indian woman** to win an **Olympic medal**.
 
• She accomplished this feat during the** 2000 Sydney Olympics**, where she won **a bronze medal** in the **women's 69 kg weightlifting **category.
 
• This landmark achievement marked a significant milestone in the history of Indian women participating in international sports events.
 
• Karnam Malleswari's success sent a strong message to Indian women, encouraging them to pursue sports actively and professionally.
 
• Her win paved the way for more Indian women athletes to aim for success in the Olympic Games and has been a source of inspiration to many Indian sportswomen who succeeded her.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirabai Chanu:**

 
 
• Mirabai Chanu is an accomplished **Indian weightlifter.**
 
• At the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**, she won a **silver medal** in the **Women's 49 kg category**.
 
• This was India's **first medal in the event** and also made her the **second Indian woman weightlifter to win an Olympic medal** after Karnam Malleswari.
 
 
 
• **PV Sindhu:**
 
 
• PV Sindhu is a **professional badminton player **from India.
 
• She made history when she became the** first Indian woman to win a silver **medal in the** 2016 Rio Olympics **in the singles badminton event.
 
• She also clinched a **bronze medal in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics **making her the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals.
 
 
 
• **Saina Nehwal:**
 
 
• Saina Nehwal is an Indian **professional badminton singles player.**
 
• She was the** first Indian badminton player** to win an Olympic medal, **a bronze**, in the **2012 London Olympics.**
 
• Nehwal has several other accomplishments, including being the first Indian to win the BWF World Championships and the first Indian woman to reach the **World No.1 ranking.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about ‘abolition of title’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 18.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 18** of the Indian Constitution discusses the** 'abolition of titles'.**
 
• Within this article, it is expressed that the **State cannot confer any titles, and citizens of India cannot accept titles from a foreign State.**
 
• This Article is integral to the** principle of equality** that the Constitution of India strongly advocates.
 
• It is meant to preserve and promote the notion of **equal recognition and respect for all citizens, irrespective of their socioeconomic status.**
 
• However, this **does not apply to academic or military distinctions.** So, educational and military awards are allowed to be employed and do not come under the purview of Article 18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 20:**

 
 
• Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides **safeguards to individuals with respect to conviction for offences.**
 
• It grants three main rights: protection from ex post facto laws, prohibition of double jeopardy, and protection against self-incrimination.
 
• These rights are considered fundamental as they safeguard **individual liberties from arbitrary encroachment by the state.**
 
 
 
• **Article 19:**
 
 
• Article 19 gives all citizens the **right to freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.**
 
• It is instrumental in maintaining the democratic fabric of the nation, as it ensures the fundamental freedoms necessary for individuals to question, articulate and participate in the governing process.
 
• However, these freedoms **come with reasonable restrictions** mentioned in the constitution itself** to maintain public order, decency or morality, and national security.**
 
 
 
• **Article 17:**
 
 
• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution **abolishes "untouchability",** and its practice in any form is forbidden.
 
• This provision comes under the **Right to Equality**, embodying the fight **against social discrimination.**
 
• It was an essential step towards an inclusive society and eliminating caste-based discrimination. Violation of this Article is punishable in accordance with the law.

questions.question: What is humidity?

options.text: When the water vapour transfers into water from air
When water vapour is present in the air
When the other gases transfer to air
When air is present in the water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When water vapour is present in the air.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Humidity** refers to the **presence of water vapour in the air.**
 
• It is an essential measurement in meteorology and is **vital to weather forecasts and climatic conditions.**
 
• The level of humidity has implications for human comfort and health.
 
• **High humidity** can make **temperatures feel warmer** than they are, while **low humidity **can result in **dry skin and other discomforts.**
 
• There are different methods to measure humidity such as **absolute humidity, relative humidity, and specific humidity**.
 
• **Relative humidity,** which is the ratio of the amount of water vapour in the air at a certain temperature to the maximum amount that the air can hold at that temperature, is the most commonly used.
 
• Understanding humidity is crucial in various fields, such as** aviation, construction, HVAC systems design, painting & coating**, and even in understanding the spread and intensity of certain infectious diseases.

questions.question: During which festival is Garba performed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Navratri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Navratri **typically involves the **worship of the goddess Durga**, commemorated in nine different forms over the course of the festival.
 
• **Garba** is a popular folk dance native to** Gujarat**, a state in western India.
 
• Its performance is central to** Navratri celebrations in Gujarat **and is now popular all over India and among Indian communities worldwide.
 
• **Beyond Navratri,** Garba is also performed during **other special occasions **in Gujarat, indicating its cultural importance.
 
• The tradition of Garba, along with another dance form called **Raas,** is also being promoted to wider audiences, demonstrating the cultural heritage of Gujarat and fostering community ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pongal:**

 
 
• Pongal is a major** harvest festival **celebrated in **Tamil Nadu**, a southern state in India. It typically falls in **mid-January**.
 
• The festival is named after the Tamil word **"pongal,"** which means **"to boil over,"** symbolizing **prosperity and abundance.**
 
• It is traditionally marked by cooking a special dish called 'Pongal' - made from **newly-harvested rice boiled in milk with jaggery**.
 
 
 
• **Diwali:**
 
 
• Diwali, also known as **Deepavali,** is a major Hindu festival celebrated by millions worldwide.
 
• Known as the **"festival of lights," **it symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil.
 
• The festival involves** lighting lamps and fireworks, decorating homes, feasting on sweets, and exchanging gifts.**
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• Bihu is a set of three important cultural festivals celebrated in **Assam,** a northeastern state in India.
 
• These festivals, celebrated throughout the year, mark the changing seasons and are **significant for agriculture.**
 
• The most recognized Bihu, Rongali Bihu, celebrates the onset of the **Assamese New Year **and the spring season.
 
• Bihu dance and music are integral parts of the celebrations, and these have become emblematic of Assamese culture.

questions.question: In December 2021, the Supreme Court suspended OBC quotas for local body elections in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **December 2021**, the Supreme Court of India **suspended the OBC** (Other Backward Classes) **quota in local body elections**.
 
• The states affected were **Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• This ruling translates to the fact that state election commissions can no longer reserve seats for OBCs in all future local body elections across India.
 
• The condition to reinstate quotas is to comply with the **Supreme Court's triple-test guidelines** which include establishing the backwardness of class, inadequacy of representation and overall efficiency.
 
• This decision has **caused significant debate regarding reservation policies** in local governance and their overall impact on social justice and representation.

questions.question: This festival was started by the Government of Nagaland In 2000 to encourage interaction among tribes and to promote the cultural heritage of the State. Identify the festival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hornbill festival.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hornbill festival** was started by the **Government of Nagaland in 2000**.
 
• The objective of the festival is** to encourage interaction among the various tribes of Nagaland.**
 
• It also aims to **promote and preserve the cultural heritage** and traditions of the state.
 
• It is sometimes referred to as the **"festival of festivals"** because it represents all the ethnic tribes in Nagaland.
 
• The Hornbill Festival is celebrated from **1st to 10th December **every year and has been highly successful.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nazu festival:**

 
 
• The Nazu festival is a major celebration among the **Pochury tribe of Nagaland**.
 
• This **pre-sowing festival** takes place for 10 days before the sowing season begins, typically in **February**.
 
• It is marked by **merrymaking, songs, dances, and games**.
 
 
 
• **Gaan-Ngai festival:**
 
 
• Gaan-Ngai is the biggest festival of the **Zeliangrong community**.
 
• The Zeliangrong community is a conglomeration of three tribes: **Zeme, Liangmai, and Rongmei,** found in North-Eastern states of India, primarily **Nagaland, Manipur, and Assam**.
 
• This** post-harvest festival **happens in December/January and stretches for **five days**.
 
• It involves various traditional rituals and **colourful cultural performances**.
 
 
 
• **Nuakhai festival:**
 
 
• Nuakhai is an **agricultural festival **celebrated primarily in the **Western part of Odisha **to mark the arrival of the **new rice harvest.**
 
• It's a significant social/communal gathering where the goddesses are invoked before the first grain of new crop.
 
• The new harvest is celebrated with **dances, songs, and a variety of local cuisines.**

questions.question: How many industries were listed in Schedule A of Industrial Policy, 1956?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** in India classified industries into three categories: **Schedule A, B, and C**.
 
• There were 1**7 industries listed under Schedule A.**
 
• The industries under Schedule A were the ones where the **state would have exclusive responsibility**.
 
• The purpose of such categorization was to help in the **systematic development** of various sectors in India.
 
• Some of the sectors under Schedule A included **arms and ammunition, atomic energy, iron and steel, heavy machinery, mineral oil, coal, etc.**
 
• The Initiative was a part of India's broader** 'socialistic pattern of society' **approach where the state played a dominant role in industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Schedule B:**

 
 
• Schedule B consisted of **12 industries.**
 
• These industries were to be progressively **state-owned, but private enterprise** could also supplement the effort.
 
• This schedule included industries such as **aluminium and other non-ferrous metals, machine tools, electrical engineering, automobiles and tractors, industrial and agricultural chemicals, and more**.
 
 
 
• **Schedule C:**
 
 
• Schedule C covered the** rest of the industries,** and they were left **open to the private sector, **although the state could also venture.
 
• This implied that the** rest of the industries not specified in Schedule A or B** could be initiated and operated by private enterprises.
 
• The government could also start any new industry in this category, depending on the national interest.
 
 

This policy intended to maintain a** balance between public and private sectors,** providing ample opportunities for private entities while the State assumed responsibility for industrial development in certain sectors.

questions.question:

b) Maldives

c) Bhutan

d) Bangladesh
questions.solution:

__
 
• According to the** latest HDI report**, **Sri Lanka** has the highest rank among the four countries, with an HDI value of 0.782 and a rank of **73 **out of 191 countries. It falls under the high human development category.
 
• **Maldives** has the second highest rank among the four countries, with an HDI value of 0.743 and a rank of **90** out of 191 countries. It also falls under the high human development category.
 
• **Bhutan **has the third highest rank among the four countries, with an HDI value of 0.654 and a rank of **127 **out of 191 countries. It falls under the medium human development category.
 
• **Bangladesh** has the lowest rank among the four countries, with an HDI value of 0.647 and a rank of **129** out of 191 countries. It also falls under the medium human development category.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI): **

 
 
• **India ranked 132 out of 191** countries in the **2021 human development index.**
 
• The report was released by the** United Nations Development Program(UNDP).**
 
• The Human Development Index was created to emphasize that people's social and economic factors should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country, not economic growth alone. 
 
• UNDP was established in the year 1965.
 
• The main goal of UNDP is to help proper nations develop Their Human and Natural resources more fully.
 
• The UNDP projects provide support to every economic and social sector of the Agriculture Industry, Education and Science, Health and Social welfare, etc.
 
• Its headquarters is located in New York.

questions.question: Asansol, Howrah, Malda and Sealdah division come under which railway zone of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eastern Railway.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asansol, Howrah, Malda, and Sealdah** divisions come under the **Eastern Railway zone of India**.
 
• The Eastern Railway is one of the **19 railway zones** in India.
 
• It is **headquartered at Fairley Place, Kolkata**.
 
• These divisions, like others in the Indian Railways, each have a **Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) **who reports to the General Manager of the zone.
 
• These divisions primarily manage the operations and maintenance of the railways** under their jurisdiction**.
 
• Eastern Railway is one of the earliest zones established by the Indian Railways and is important for passenger and freight transportation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian Railways is **one of the largest rail networks** in the world. It spans **over 68,000 km,** connecting almost every major city and town in India.
 
• **As of 2025,** the Indian Railways is organized into **19 zones,** which are further divided into a total of **70 divisions.** Each zone is headed by a General Manager, and the divisions are managed by Divisional Railway Managers.
 
• These zones were mostly reorganized based on **linguistic and operational feasibility**.
 
• Some of the major zones include the** Northern Railway (headquartered in Delhi), Western Railway (headquartered in Mumbai), Eastern Railway (headquartered in Kolkata), and Southern Railway (headquartered in Chennai)**.
 
• The Indian Railways plays a key role in India's economy and is a significant employer. It has over **1.4 million employees** and contributes to both passenger transport and freight operations in the country.
 
• Indian Railways has been integrating technology into its operations to improve **efficiency and user experience**. This includes computerized ticket booking, live tracking of trains, digital payments, and an online complaint management system.

questions.question: What cells help In osmoregulation In platyhelminthes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flame cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flame cells** are specialized cells that form** part of the excretory system** in these organisms, known as **protonephridia.**
 
• Flame cells play a primary** role in osmoregulation,** the process by which a balance of water and ions is maintained within the body.
 
• Along with osmoregulation, flame cells also help in the **removal of waste products**.
 
• This system is not only found in Platyhelminthes but **also in other types of flatworms and invertebrates**. However, it is most prominent in **Platyhelminthes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nerve cells:**

 
 
• Platyhelminthes have a decentralized nerve cell network and two longitudinal nerve cords running along their body length.
 
• These nerve cells, also known as **neurons**, are responsible for **transmitting signals** across the organism.
 
• They enable **sensing the environment and coordinating the organism's **response to it.
 
 
 
• **Ganglia:**
 
 
• Ganglia are simple forms of** "brains"** or collections of nerve cell bodies that process information in invertebrates such as **Platyhelminthes**.
 
• They serve as the **central nervous system** in these organisms, acting as control centres that coordinate nerve signals.
 
 
 
• **Hooks:**
 
 
• Some Platyhelminthes, specifically parasitic ones, have **hooks and suckers**.
 
• These structures are **not cells, **but adaptations that help the worm to attach to the host's tissue.
 
• The hooks **assist in anchoring the parasite** to its host and facilitate the feeding process.

questions.question: Who among the following is associated with the musical instrument Surbahar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annapurna Devi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annapurna Devi** is associated with the musical instrument **Surbahar.**
 
• Annapurna Devi was an Indian surbahar player of **Hindustani classical music**.
 
• She was also a renowned music teacher in the **Maihar gharana, **a school of Hindustani classical music.
 
• She was one of the most respected and eminent musicians of the **20th century in India**.
 
• The **Surbahar is a stringed instrument **often described as the **bass sitar,** and it is primarily used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Annapurna Devi's mastery of the Surbahar contributed significantly to the popularity and recognition of the instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiv Kumar Sharma:**

 
 
• Shiv Kumar Sharma is an iconic Indian music composer and **santoor player,** and he is largely responsible for making the santoor a popular Classical instrument.
 
• He was **born in Jammu** and brought the tradition of playing the s**antoor, hitherto** a folk instrument of Jammu and Kashmir, to the Indian classical music mainstream.
 
• Sharma has composed music for many Hindi films in** collaboration with Hariprasad Chaurasia**, forming a **group called Shiv-Hari**.
 
 
 
• **Sharan Rani:**
 
 
• Sharan Rani was an Indian classical **Sarod player** and she is often referred to as the** 'Sarod Rani'**.
 
• Rani made a significant contribution to popularising Indian classical music and was one of the few famous women instrumentalists in the **mid-20th century**.
 
• She was also the first internationally acclaimed woman performer on the Sarod.

questions.question: President Ram Nath Kovind conferred which award on Matha B Manjamma for Jogati Nrithyaa in 2021?

questions.question: Ferns, horsetails and lycophytes belong to which of the following groups?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pteridophyta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferns, horsetails, and lycophytes** all belong to the group referred to as **Pteridophyta.**
 
• These represent some of the** earlier forms of vascular plants on Earth.**
 
• They are classified as a subdivision of the plant kingdom, known as **cryptogams,** which **do not produce seeds or flowers.**
 
• Pteridophyta plants** reproduce via spores, **which are usually located on the underside of the fronds (leaves) in organs or structures called **sporangia.**
 
• The life cycle of Pteridophytes includes two distinct phases – **the large, prominent sporophyte and a less visible**, but still independent gametophyte also known as a **prothallium.**
 
• These plants are typically found in damp, shaded areas, though some have adapted to a variety of other habitats. Ferns, in particular, are known for their feather-like fronds and intricate patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophyta:**

 
 
• Bryophyta constitute the group of plants known as mosses and liverworts.
 
• They often grow in moist, shaded areas and are non-vascular, meaning they lack tissues for transporting water and nutrients.
 
• Unlike ferns, mosses reproduce using spores but are more primitive, often growing low to the ground.
 
 
 
• **Algae:**
 
 
• Algae is a diverse group of aquatic, photosynthetic organisms.
 
• They form a crucial part of the food chain in aquatic ecosystems and can range from microscopic sizes (microalgae) to massive kelp.
 
• Algae is not a homogeneous group but a term used to describe organisms from different evolutionary backgrounds that share some common features.
 
 
 
• **Fungi:**
 
 
• Fungi are a kingdom of usually multicellular eukaryotic organisms which are heterotrophic, meaning they obtain nutrients by consuming organic matter.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling in ecosystems and include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• Some fungi form symbiotic relationships with plants, aiding in nutrient absorption, while others can be pathogenic, causing diseases in plants and animals.

questions.question: The Ashtadhyayi of Panini is a renowned work on _______.

__
 
• **Ashtadhyayi**, also known as Astadhyayi, is a renowned work on **Sanskrit Grammar.**
 
• This treatise was written by the ancient Indian grammarian** Panini** between the** 6th and 5th century BC.**
 
• It set the linguistic standards for** Classical Sanskrit** and is deemed to be the earliest systematic grammar of Sanskrit.
 
• Ashtadhyayi is composed of approximately **4,000 sutras **and is organized into eight chapters, hence the name "Ashtadhyayi," which translates to** "Eight Chapters."**
 
• This work not only covers grammar but also incorporates the science of** phonetics**, particularly as it was understood within the ancient **Vedic tradition.​**

questions.question: M₂, is one of the measures of money supply. M₂ is the sum of M₁+ ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**saving deposits with post office.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• M₂ includes all components of M₁ (which comprises currency in the hands of the public and demand deposits, or other liquid deposits), plus** savings deposits** (including money market deposit accounts), small-denomination time deposits (certificates of deposit, or CDs, of under $100,000), and retail (small-denomination) money market mutual fund shares.
 
• These elements are seen as** "near money"** and can be readily converted to cash, therefore, they are included in the broader measure of the money supply known as M₂.
 
• **Post office savings** are included as they are a **type of savings deposit.** National Saving Certificates, coins and currency notes, and demand deposits are not added to M₁ to get M₂, as these are either already accounted for in M₁ or are different form of savings assets.
 
• Please note that exact components of M₂ **may vary slightly between different countries** depending on their banking and financial systems.

questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act enacted in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Vernacular Press Act** was enacted in British India in the year** 1878.**
 
• This law was enforced by the British **to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press.**
 
• The Act was used to **prevent the expression of criticism **toward British policies, notably, the opposition that had grown with the outset of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878-80)
 
• It was enacted when** Lord Lytton **was Viceroy of India; he was known for his **controversial and suppressive policies** during his tenure.
 
• The act stated that any press printing in Vernacular language had to declare all its printing machinery and submit all material for scrutiny before publication. If the content was inflammable or criticised British authorities, it would result in the confiscation of the press.
 
• It was the **first legislation to curtail press freedom in India,** and the press became a medium of both control and revolt during British rule.
 
• The act** provoked widespread criticism and protest by Indians.** It eventually became one of the contributing factors to the nationalistic movements that emerged at the **end of the 19th century.**
 
• The Act was, however**, repealed in 1882 by Lytton's successor, Lord Ripon,** in a move to foster press freedom in India.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct Lewis structure of O₃? 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/276363878e0f4caa97cab6cfd01eac9bf4c1f0c46d1bf0866a0d962519dac8bd.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**d.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Each of the three oxygen atoms in an** O₃** molecule has** six valence electrons.** This totals 18 valence electrons for the molecule.
 
• In the central oxygen atom,** two bonds are formed:** one with each of the two other Oxygen atoms.
 
• It utilizes 4 out of 18 electrons, leaving us with 14 electrons.
 
• The rest of the **14 electrons are distributed as lone pairs.** Each oxygen atom receives three lone pairs (2 electrons form a pair), which account for 6 x 3 = 18 electrons. This includes the electrons shared in the bonds.
 
• But for total 18 electrons, two electrons are needed from somewhere else.
 
• These electron pair is provided by another oxygen atom, forming a double bond between the central oxygen and one of the peripheral oxygen atoms.

So, the **Lewis structure of O3 **can be denoted as** O-O=O**, where** "-" denotes a single bond containing 2 electrons and "=" denotes a double bond which contains 4 electrons. One oxygen forms a single bond with the central oxygen, while another forms a double bond. Each oxygen atom also has 6 electrons (or 3 pairs) forming lone pairs around them.**
